_about: Rivals in Tycoon Town: a business like one of yours opens close by and takes some of its customers. names = two rival names per business (used in turn). cases = what to do about it, one for each kind of business (for: food, shop, service, property, big = Downtown and Skyline businesses). Options follow content/FORMAT.md, plus shield (0 to 0.6): how much of the rival's pull the choice blocks; a well-shielded business also makes the rival close sooner. In the words, {rival} is the rival's name, {biz} your business (lower case), {where} where the rival opened (right next door, just across the street, a few doors away).

cases.title: A rival opens {where}
cases.story: {rival} just opened {where}, selling food just like your {biz}. Some of your customers are trying it out. What will you do?

options.text: Make your food even better and greet every customer by name
options.result: Customers taste the difference and come back. {rival} struggles to keep up with you.
options.lesson: Beat a rival by being better, not just cheaper.

options.text: Start a stamp card: every 10th treat is free
options.result: Regulars collect stamps and keep coming to you instead of {rival}.
options.lesson: Loyal customers are hard for a rival to steal.

options.text: Cut all your prices in half to drive them out
options.result: {rival} cuts prices too. You both sell lots and earn almost nothing.
options.lesson: A price war hurts everyone. Profit, not sales, pays the bills.

options.text: Tell everyone their food made people sick (it did not)
options.result: {rival} complains, the council fines you for spreading lies, and customers stop trusting you.
options.lesson: Lying about a rival is unfair, and it can get you fined.

options.text: Do nothing and hope they go away
options.result: {rival} keeps taking some of your customers, month after month.
options.lesson: Ignoring competition rarely makes it disappear.

cases.title: A new shop {where}
cases.story: {rival} opened {where}, selling the same kinds of things as your {biz}. Fewer people are coming through your door. What is your plan?

options.text: Stock things {rival} does not have and show them off
options.result: Shoppers come to you for things they cannot find anywhere else.
options.lesson: Be different: give customers a reason to choose you.

options.text: Give friendly expert advice and free gift wrapping
options.result: People like how helpful you are and tell their friends.
options.lesson: Great service is something a rival cannot copy overnight.

options.text: Open an online shop as well
options.result: Customers who never walk past your street start ordering from you.
options.lesson: Reach customers in more than one way.

options.text: Copy everything they sell, but cheaper
options.result: {rival} drops its prices again and you both earn less.
options.lesson: Copying a rival makes you the same, only poorer.

options.text: Pay someone to post fake bad reviews about them
options.result: The review site finds out, deletes them and names your shop. You pay a fine and lose trust.
options.lesson: Fake reviews are cheating, and they usually get found out.

cases.title: Competition {where}
cases.story: {rival} has opened {where}, offering the same service as your {biz}. Some of your regulars have gone to try them. What do you do?

options.text: Ask customers what they want and make your service the best
options.result: You fix the little things customers mentioned. They notice, and stay.
options.lesson: Listen to customers: they tell you how to win.

options.text: Offer a membership deal for regular customers
options.result: Members keep coming back every month, whatever {rival} does.
options.lesson: Regular customers give you steady money.

options.text: Hand out leaflets with a one-week offer
options.result: A busy week, then things go back to how they were.
options.lesson: A quick offer helps for a moment. A better service lasts.

options.text: Work much longer hours for less money to undercut them
options.result: Your team gets tired and grumpy, and customers notice.
options.lesson: Tired people do worse work. Compete on quality, not exhaustion.

options.text: Rip down their posters around town at night
options.result: A camera films you. You pay for the damage and it is all over town.
options.lesson: Damaging a rival's things is wrong, and it always costs you.

cases.title: New building {where}
cases.story: {rival}, a brand-new building, opened {where}. Some of your tenants are thinking about moving there. What do you do?

options.text: Fix things fast and make the shared spaces lovely
options.result: Tenants love living and working in your building and decide to stay.
options.lesson: Happy tenants stay. Moving out costs them time and money too.

options.text: Offer a small discount to tenants who stay two more years
options.result: Most tenants sign up. A little less rent, but no empty rooms.
options.lesson: A full building with fair rent beats a pricey empty one.

options.text: Paint the front and put up a big new sign
options.result: It looks nicer for a while, but tenants care more about what is inside.
options.lesson: Looks help, but quality keeps customers.

options.text: Raise the rent to make up for the tenants who left
options.result: Even more tenants leave for {rival}. The building gets emptier.
options.lesson: Charging more when customers have a choice drives them away.

options.text: Tell tenants the new building is unsafe (it is not)
options.result: The owners of {rival} take you to court for telling lies, and you pay.
options.lesson: Scaring people with lies is wrong, and it can cost a lot.

cases.title: A big rival arrives
cases.story: {rival}, a big company, opened {where} and wants the same customers as your {biz}. Its adverts are everywhere. What is your plan?

options.text: Invest in what makes you special and tell customers about it
options.result: Customers see why you are worth choosing, and {rival} cannot match it.
options.lesson: Know your strengths and make them even stronger.

options.text: Sign long contracts with your best customers at a fair price
options.result: Your biggest customers stay with you for years.
options.lesson: Long, fair deals make your income steady.

options.text: Train your staff and pay them well so the best people stay
options.result: {rival} tries to hire your team, but they are happy where they are.
options.lesson: Great people are a company's best defence.

options.text: Sell below cost for a year to push them out
options.result: {rival} has more money than you, waits it out, and you lose a fortune.
options.lesson: Never start a price war you cannot afford to finish.

options.text: Secretly agree with {rival} that you both raise prices
options.result: That is price-fixing. The government finds out and fines you both a lot.
options.lesson: Rivals agreeing on prices is against the law. It cheats customers.
